description: The line plot illustrates the performance of three variants of the DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) model, measured by MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10), as a function of the number of queries used during inference (S), ranging from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S),” is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at each whole number from 1 to 10. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10,” spans from 33.0 to 36.0 in increments of 0.5. The black solid line, labeled “DPR w/o query,” represents a baseline with no query expansion and remains constant at approximately 34.2 across all values of S. The red line with circular markers, labeled “DPR w/ corpus expansion,” starts at 35.1 when S=1, rises to a peak of 35.8 at S=6, and then plateaus slightly around 35.7–35.8 through S=10. The green line with triangular markers, labeled “DPR w/ document expansion,” begins at 34.8, dips slightly to 34.7 at S=3, then rises to 34.9 at S=5, and gradually declines to 34.8 at S=10. The blue line with star markers, also labeled “DPR w/ document expansion” in the legend (likely a labeling error, as it visually differs from the green line), starts at 34.8, peaks at 35.0 at S=2, dips to 34.6 at S=6, and continues declining to 34.4 at S=10. The plot suggests that corpus expansion consistently outperforms the other methods across all S values, while document expansion shows mixed or declining performance depending on the specific variant represented.
